html: Core ability, Start of Any Turn. A friendly Hero within 3" of a Place of Power rolls a dice: on a 1 it suffers D3 mortal damage; on a 2+ a Wizard or Priest adds 1 to casting/chanting rolls this turn, and any other Hero can use ‘Unbind’ or ‘Banish Manifestation’ this turn as if it had Wizard (1).
Terrain type. Hills and similar features. Has the Cover terrain ability.
An ability keyword carried by abilities that make attacks, such as ‘Shoot’ and ‘Fight’. Reactions such as ‘All-out Attack’ and ‘All-out Defence’ are used in response to Attack abilities.
Weapon characteristic. The number of attacks each model makes with that weapon (one hit roll per attack).
Roll of 2D6 made as part of ‘Banish Manifestation’. If it equals or beats the banishment value on the manifestation’s warscroll, the manifestation is banished and removed from play.
An ability keyword carried by ‘Banish Manifestation’. Using a Banish ability counts towards a Wizard or Priest’s power level for the phase.
A faction rule picked during army composition. You pick 1 battle formation for your army; it gives your army an extra ability or rule.
A unit keyword. Animals and creatures that fight without riders. Some abilities can only affect, or cannot affect, Beasts.
Roll of 2D6 made to cast a spell. If it equals or beats the spell’s casting value, the spell is successfully cast (unless it is unbound). A roll with two or more 1s is a miscast.
The fifth phase of a turn. The active player’s units can use ‘Charge’ abilities to move into combat.
Roll of 2D6 made when a unit uses a ‘Charge’ ability. The unit can move up to that many inches and must end within ½" of an enemy unit.

Roll of a D6 made to chant a prayer. On an unmodified 1 the prayer fails and the Priest loses D3 ritual points. On a 2+ either bank the roll as ritual points, or add the Priest’s ritual points to the roll and, if it equals or beats the chanting value, the prayer is answered (ritual points then reset to 0).

The sixth phase of a turn. The active player uses Combat Phase abilities that are not Fight abilities, then their opponent does the same; then players alternate picking units to use a Fight ability, starting with the active player. Each unit must fight if it is able to.
An ability keyword carried by abilities used to set up units during the deployment phase. Players alternate using Deploy abilities until both armies are set up.
An ability keyword carried by abilities used to set up faction terrain features. In the deployment phase, the player who begins deployment uses their Deploy Terrain abilities first.
The last phase of each turn. Abilities with an End of Turn timing are used, objective control is checked and many score-related effects happen.

A keyword and terrain type. A terrain feature with its own warscroll that belongs to a faction. It is set up with a Deploy Terrain ability and cannot be picked as the target of some abilities (e.g. ‘Covering Fire’).
Rolling the dice for several attacks with the same characteristics at the same time instead of one at a time, to speed up play.

A unit keyword. Leaders and champions. Every regiment is led by a Hero, your general must be a Hero, all Heroes have the ‘Guarded Hero’ passive ability and most enhancements can only be given to Heroes.
The second phase of a turn. Spells and prayers are usually used in their commander’s hero phase, as are commands such as ‘Rally’.
Weapon characteristic. The number you need to equal or beat on a hit roll for an attack to score a hit.
The first step of the attack sequence. Roll a dice; if it equals or beats the weapon’s Hit characteristic, the attack scores a hit. An unmodified 1 always fails; an unmodified 6 is a critical hit.
Terrain ability. Models cannot move across, be set up on or end moves on any part of this terrain feature.
A weapon used to make combat attacks with the ‘Fight’ ability. The attacking model must be within the weapon’s range of the target (usually its combat range).

A unit keyword for endless spells and invocations. Manifestations have their own warscrolls and are treated as units for many rules (movement, combat range, being targeted, taking damage), but not all. If the Wizard or Priest that summoned one is slain, it is removed from the battlefield.
An ability keyword carried by abilities that move a unit, such as ‘Normal Move’, ‘Run’, ‘Retreat’ and ‘Charge’.
The third phase of a turn. The active player’s units can use ‘Normal Move’, ‘Run’ or ‘Retreat’.
Terrain type. Ruins, debris, barricades and similar features. Has the Cover and Unstable terrain abilities.
Terrain type. Wyldwoods, fortress walls and similar features. Has the Cover, Obscuring and Unstable terrain abilities.
Ability timing restriction. A unit can use the ability at most once in that phase, turn or battle. With ‘(Army)’ added, the ability can be used only once in that window across your whole army.
Terrain ability and terrain type. Heroes within 3" of this terrain feature can use the ‘Activate Place of Power’ ability.

Command, End of Any Turn. A unit that charged this turn inflicts D3 mortal damage on an enemy unit in combat with it that has a lower Health characteristic, then can move through that enemy’s combat range.
The roll-off at the start of each battle round after the first. The winner decides who takes the first turn; on a tie, the player who went first in the previous battle round decides.
The 6 dice rolled for the ‘Rally’ command. Each 4+ gives 1 rally point to spend on healing or returning slain models.
A weapon used to make shooting attacks with the ‘Shoot’ ability. The target must be visible and within the weapon’s Range characteristic.
Rolling some or all of the dice of a roll again. A dice cannot be re-rolled more than once, and re-rolls happen before modifiers are applied.

A unit cannot use more than 1 Core ability per phase, cannot use the same ability more than once per phase (unless specified otherwise), and cannot be affected by the same passive ability more than once at the same time.
Roll of a D6 made as part of a ‘Run’ ability; add it to the unit’s Move characteristic for that move.

The third step of the attack sequence. The defender rolls a dice and subtracts the weapon’s Rend; if the result equals or beats the target’s Save characteristic, the attack is blocked. An unmodified 1 always fails.
The separate parts that some terrain features are made of (e.g. a set of ruins). All of a terrain feature’s scenery pieces together count as 1 terrain feature.
If the Wizard or Priest that summoned a manifestation is slain, that manifestation is removed from the battlefield.
An attack made with a ranged weapon. Units cannot use ‘Shoot’ while in combat unless the weapon has Shoot in Combat.
The fourth phase of a turn. The active player’s units that did not Run or Retreat this turn can use the ‘Shoot’ ability.

Before any turns in a battle round: determine the active player (priority roll after the first round), determine the underdog, then each player can use Start of Battle Round abilities, active player first.
The first phase of each turn. Abilities with a Start of Turn timing (e.g. ‘Activate Place of Power’, ‘Tactical Gambit’) are used here.
Terrain features can be controlled like objectives, but control is lost as soon as no friendly models are contesting them.
Small: fits in 7" × 7". Medium: not small and fits in 7" × 12". Large: anything bigger.
Roll of 2D6 made as part of ‘Unbind’. If it beats the casting roll, the spell fails.
A keyword on some spells and prayers. Normally no more than 1 friendly Wizard can cast the same spell (or 1 Priest chant the same prayer) per turn; Unlimited spells and prayers ignore that limit.
Part of a reaction’s rules text that says which unit uses the reaction (e.g. ‘The unit using that Attack ability’).
Points scored as set out in the battleplan. The player with the most at the end of the battle wins; the player with the fewest at the start of a battle round is the underdog.
A unit keyword. Artillery pieces, engines and other constructs. Some rules treat War Machines differently from other units.
Roll of a dice made for each damage point inflicted on a unit with Ward, before it is allocated. If it equals or beats the Ward value, that damage point is negated.
A unit keyword. If any units in your army have Warmaster, you must pick one of them to be your general.
Weapon characteristic. The number you need to equal or beat on a wound roll for a hit to wound the target.
The second step of the attack sequence. For each hit, roll a dice; if it equals or beats the weapon’s Wound characteristic, the attack wounds. An unmodified 1 always fails.
Points a Priest builds up from chanting rolls and can later add to a chanting roll to answer a prayer. They can be accumulated over multiple turns.
